justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Chronic pain and anxiety reduction consistent across studies; cancer fatigue and LBP best-evidenced conditions.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: 800-hour training program required; multi-year commitment; significant time and cost.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to chronic pain, stress, and movement disorders; growing in integrative health settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Very limited insurance coverage; primarily self-pay; some integrative health and wellness policies offer partial coverage.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Limited employer demand in clinical settings; primarily self-employed or integrative wellness practice.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Very high; mind-body approach appeals to patients seeking holistic care.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Wellness-oriented consumers readily pay cash for yoga therapy, especially in chronic pain, stress, and oncology niches.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: IAYT is the recognized credential but competes with abundant yoga teachers; premium pricing possible only in clinical/medical positioning.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: C-IAYT is comparatively rare among PTs/OTs, providing real differentiation in integrative health markets.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Group classes and small-group programming scale beyond the owner, though credentialed therapists are limited.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Strong consumer recognition of yoga; 'yoga therapy' as a clinical service is less recognized but growing.
justifications.business.efficiency: 800+ hour training over 2-3 years and several thousand dollars; slow and expensive ROI.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Not recognized for tenure/promotion at PT/OT programs; viewed as adjunct wellness training.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Modest but growing literature base; some integrative health journals publish yoga therapy research.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Limited curricular fit; may inform wellness or integrative health electives.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Mixed evidence; reasonable RCTs in low back pain and anxiety, weaker elsewhere.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Essentially never listed in PT/OT faculty postings.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Long, expensive training with minimal academic return.
